image_policy.image_generation_notes: Use the visual to reduce load by making the integral-as-area idea explicit. Keep the base case rectangular and avoid decorative signal art.

tutorial_outline.direct_instruction_goal: Teach that once a convolution has been broken into time regions, each regional integral can be evaluated by finding the area of the shaded product region in \tau.
tutorial_outline.base_case: Use a single overlap interval where x(\tau)h(t - \tau) is constant, so the convolution contribution is a rectangle area.
paragraph_plan: Start from the convolution integral and state that t is fixed while \tau is the horizontal variable used to measure overlap.
Explain that each time region gives one nonzero product shape, and the integral over that shape is the area of the shaded region.
Use the image to connect support overlap, product height, and geometric area in the simplest constant-height case.
Preview that later sections use the same area idea for rectangles, triangles, trapezoids, composite regions, and final piecewise assembly.
display_math_plan: Display a one-region setup y(t) = \int_{a(t)}^{b(t)} x(\tau)h(t - \tau)\,d\tau.
Display the constant-height area shortcut \int_{a(t)}^{b(t)} C\,d\tau = C(b(t) - a(t)).
